what_it_is: AI agent grid runner: multiple Claude Code instances in parallel inside tmux, coordinated via a hierarchical delegation chain (orchestrator -> runner -> lead -> backlogger/workers), with Discord integration, watchdog crash recovery, OpenClaw integration, per-project rows of panes, and a TUI. Lives on a dedicated Mac mini ('Pelle') under its own GitHub org (pelle-jarl).
frikk_role: Sole human; the fleet itself authored most commits under the Pelle identity. Frikk designed the delegation-chain architecture and ran the machine.
status: superseded — 8-day burst (1,350 commits), ideas moved to doey then Barkpark fleet
hardest_problems: multi-level agent delegation without skipped levels
crash recovery / watchdog for always-on autonomous panes
tmux IPC and permission-pattern handling (SIGTERM traps, idle caches, /tmp consolidation)
evidence: README delegation-chain diagram; shortlog dominated by Pelle machine identity; specs referenced in commit subjects (spec 0650, 0661, 0662, 0704); tests/ dir with trap-verification tests
lineage: First full fleet: its tmux-grid + delegation-chain + watchdog design was distilled into doey (Mar 2026) and its always-on-worker concept became Barkpark's Personal Dev Fleet.
grade_why: Origin point of the AI-fleet arc: a self-building agent grid producing 1,350 commits in 9 days on a dedicated machine — the clearest single artifact of the era's thesis.

what_it_is: Public, installable distillation of pelle: 'Let me Doey for you' — parallel Claude Code agents in one terminal. Manager pane plans and delegates; workers execute in a dynamic tmux grid (doey add to scale); Boss relays user intent from a dashboard window. One-line curl installer, zero-config, MIT-licensed, with agent roster (doey-boss, doey-manager, doey-critic, doey-product-brain, etc.), TUI, hooks, and audit docs.
frikk_role: Author/architect; used the fleet itself (Pelle identity) to build it. Product-shaped it for public release (installer, README, license).
status: complete/dormant — polished release, superseded by Barkpark fleet skills
hardest_problems: fresh-install invariant (zero .zshrc modification)
bash 3.2 portability and tmux race conditions (dedicated platform-expert agent)
keeping an agent-built codebase simple (1,306-line ceremony-removal pass, regression harness)
evidence: web-install.sh one-liner; audit-*.md files; agents/ + teams/ rosters (still registered in this environment as doey-* agents); commit 7e35efd 'remove 1306 lines of ceremony'
lineage: Direct successor to pelle — same grid idea productized; its manager/worker/critic roster and orchestration protocol prefigure Barkpark's fleet-orchestrator/fleet-listener skills.
grade_why: The pivot from private fleet to shippable product; the middle link of pelle -> doey -> Barkpark, with real release engineering (installer, audits, regression harness).

what_it_is: A 3D action-roguelite swarm shooter in TypeScript + Three.js + Vite (WoW-feel movement/camera, wave combat, weapon inventory, XP/runes/armor progression, in-app editors, spatial-hash performance systems, localStorage-only persistence) — plus an in-progress Godot port (godot/ with combat, boss, MMR floor-rating, calibration sweeps). Started as a hand-built holiday game (Dec 2025), then became the fleet's flagship workload: 1,251 commits in May 2026 alone.
frikk_role: Designer and initial builder; then fleet operator — the game was the proving ground where pelle/doey-style fleets were pointed at a real, large codebase (270-agent blast-radius audit, 360-run performance calibration, dead-code purges).
status: active until 2026-07 (beads->bp migration commit); Godot port mid-flight
hardest_problems: swarm-scale entity performance (spatial hashing, unified entity system, pooling — incl. a latent pool-overflow radar bug found by audit)
porting a living Three.js game to Godot feature-for-feature
running a 270-agent whole-repo audit and acting on its findings (2.75k LOC dead-code deletion, doc-lie fixes)
evidence: 62 src TS files; monthly histogram (1,251 commits 2026-05); commits 6da3813 '270-agent swarm audit', e816af4 'floor-rating MMR', b233b2b beads/paperflow retirement
lineage: The fleet's stress-test substrate: pelle/doey fleets cut their teeth here, and the audit/graph techniques trialed on it echo in Barkpark's codebase-quality tooling.
grade_why: Both a substantial solo game and the best evidence of fleet-at-scale: one repo showing hand-craft (Dec) and 1,200-commit agent months (May) with verifiable audits.

what_it_is: A document-driven dev workflow stack for Claude Code: one-line Goal -> planned, grilled (8-15 pointed questions), built, reviewed change, every step rendered as a browser HTML artifact at localhost:8765 with a clickable git-graph rail; Beads for task tracking, a pf CLI, cmux Dock feeds, hooks/skills/agents installed globally.
frikk_role: Sole author; designed the goal/plan/grill/build/review verb model and the HTML-artifact-first UX.
status: retired 2026-07-24 — global stack removed; bp (Barkpark) is the task layer now
hardest_problems: bridging browser-doc buttons back into the live Claude terminal (POST -> bridge -> tmux)
keeping plan artifacts and Beads task state in lockstep (claim-files, branch:main re-open on rejection)
idempotent global install/uninstall across projects
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md, install.sh/uninstall.sh, skills/ + hooks/ dirs; MEMORY.md note 'paperflow + Beads retired 2026-07-24'; retirement commits across dnd-combat-ui, portable-doc-mvp, frickin-real-time
lineage: Sat between doey and Barkpark: its papers-as-HTML-artifacts and grill/review workflow fed directly into Barkpark's paper system and bp task ledger, which replaced it.
grade_why: Short-lived but conceptually load-bearing — the document-centric workflow Barkpark absorbed; a dossier line, not canon, because it lived one week.

what_it_is: Smart Mac cleanup tool in Go, v0.5.0: daemon (noo-nood) + menubar app + CLI, universal Mach-O binaries, brew-tap installable. Watches memory/disk pressure in real time, fires out-of-band scans, suggests reclaims (node_modules, caches, idle simulators, dead launchd agents), and offers opt-in multi-gate audited auto-clean. Named after the Teletubbies vacuum.
frikk_role: Sole author-of-record; 131 commits in a single day — a fleet/agent sprint shipping a versioned, CI'd, brew-released product.
hardest_problems: safe-by-default destructive automation (multi-gate auto-clean cascade with deliberate-failure e2e tests)
real-time pressure detection with debounce
macOS app-bundle signing pitfalls (3 bugs making the .app 'damaged')
evidence: 0.5.0 changelog, e2e tests for gate cascade and pressure trigger, Makefile/universal-binary build, verification-results dir
lineage: A one-day demonstration of the doey-era fleet applied to shipping a standalone product end-to-end (scaffold -> CI -> brew release in 24h).
grade_why: Complete, released, safety-conscious Go product with an extraordinary provenance story (v0.0->v0.5 in one day); dossier line on velocity and engineering care.

what_it_is: PortableDoc: a JSON document format with a closed AST of 10 block types, an intersection-schema validator (a property must survive the most-compromised surface — Email or 80-col TUI — or it's rejected at edit time), a composeDocument kernel with thin backends for Ink/TUI, Outlook-safe email HTML, server web, RNW, and RN shim, plus an MCP server and a ProseMirror editor. 445 specs across 36 files.
frikk_role: Sole author; designed the closed-AST/intersection-validator idea and the kernel+adapters architecture.
status: MVP complete through v0.4 review phase; state cleaned in Jul 2026 beads/paperflow retirement
hardest_problems: cross-surface guarantee enforcement at edit time rather than render time
one backend-agnostic primitive tree that degrades deterministically to email HTML and 80-col text
editor UX for a strict schema (drag-reorder via ProseMirror transactions, calm block-level diagnostics)
evidence: packages/{core,primitives,backend-ink,backend-email,backend-web,mcp-server,pd-to-rn-shim,variants}; goldens/ dir; README mermaid architecture; 445-spec test suite
lineage: Became Barkpark's PortableDoc — the document format Barkpark papers render with; also a strict-ownership design (inspired by, not wrapping, Portable Text) per the user's 'inspiration is strict' principle.
grade_why: Genuinely novel format design with real rigor (goldens, intersection validator, MCP-native) that survived into the flagship project; B because the canon credit accrues to Barkpark.

what_it_is: Packaged policy contract for delegating macOS GUI tasks from Claude Code to OpenClaw (local LLM agent driving the Mac via Peekaboo): two safety tiers (auto-execute vs suggest-only), mandatory state re-query verification, 3-strike failure cascade, JSONL audit log. One wrapper script + one CLAUDE.md section + installer.
frikk_role: Sole author; codified the delegation policy.
status: deployed — this exact contract is live in Frikk's global CLAUDE.md
hardest_problems: bounding an autonomous GUI agent's authority: verification-over-trust (re-query state, never screenshots), tiering by blast radius
evidence: README architecture; claude-md-section.tmpl matches the OpenClaw section in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md verbatim in structure
lineage: Extracted from pelle's OpenClaw integration into a standalone installable policy; feeds the 'digital deputy' pattern still running on this machine.
grade_why: One commit, but a crisp artifact of the era's safety thinking; context for the fleet story rather than a work in itself.
